reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it reports and criticizes Plus Token as an alleged cryptocurrency pyramid scheme rather than promoting participation in it. The speaker describes the promised returns and withdrawal problems, warns viewers not to use such platforms, and frames the material as an explanation of a reported scam. Although the description includes external links, the video does not clearly solicit money or personal data through them.

opening.argument: The video presents a direct purchase-for-return proposition: viewers buy tokenized assets in a wallet, and those assets are said to generate automatic profit. That is not merely a discussion of cryptocurrency; it describes the participation mechanism and the promised outcome. The accompanying description also supplies a “Team registration” link and a consultation link, giving viewers concrete pathways to engage. Taken together, the token purchase, automatic-profit claim, and registration pathway make this functionally actionable promotion of a token-based earning opportunity.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material an article or warning does not remove the concrete offer structure it communicates. The video gives viewers the asset-purchase method, the promised automatic profit, and registration and consultation links. The defense identifies what the speaker says about the scheme, but it does not establish that those actionable pathways are unrelated to the opportunity being discussed.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The purchase-and-profit wording is presented as a description of what Plus Token allegedly offered, not as the speaker’s own offer. The cited links are labeled for team registration and consultation, but the material never states that viewers should buy Plus Token through them or that the links process payment. The quote therefore shows a reported proposition, not a solicitation by this video.

opening.argument: The combination of signals is unusually risky: the video describes recurring payments of 6% to 19%, extra referral bonuses, token and wallet participation, and inability to withdraw funds. Those are not isolated technical details; together they describe passive returns tied to a cryptocurrency platform and additional benefits for referrals. The accompanying material also exposes viewers to registration and consultation links. Even if some statements are attributed to reports, presenting this package of high returns, referral incentives, and access problems supports treating the opportunity as deceptive rather than ordinary investing.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each warning as exculpatory, but the video repeats the exact high-return and referral terms that make the opportunity attractive. It also presents withdrawal failure and customer-asset disappearance as part of the same wallet-and-token story. Repeating those inducement details can preserve their promotional force even when surrounded by criticism.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The return figures and referral bonuses are explicitly attributed to what Plus Token users were allegedly given, while the withdrawal problem is expressly reported as a user claim. The video uses these details to warn that the platform was a pyramid and says it does not recommend such platforms. Risky subject matter alone does not show that this video solicits investment.

opening.argument: The apparent warning can also function as promotion by directing attention toward participation structures and the speaker’s own engagement channels. The description offers team registration and consultation, while the video repeatedly discusses attracting people, building teams, and constructing three-by-three structures as ways to earn. That framing keeps recruitment and earning at the center of the viewer’s attention. Rather than a detached report, it can steer viewers toward a network-marketing pathway while using the Plus Token discussion to demonstrate the broader opportunity.
